method: Every backbone/event/director driver->driver edge (377 after dedup) checked against source and target SSU (results/nodes_all.csv); raw per-origin weights compared before confidence-weighted dedup; 2-node cycles enumerated; path flows attributed per driver edge with market_impact.mi.graph.Network (unit shocks of all drivers, and the entry shocks of each catalogue event with clamping). Proposed scales were re-propagated: total |impact| over all 161 events falls 28,017 -> 24,816 (-11%); EV_CPI_REACCEL_SEP26 -39%, EV_OMC_FUEL_FREEZE_LOSSES -46% (non-OMC spill-over), EV_IRAN_WAR_HORMUZ_OIL -19%, EV_HORMUZ_FULL_CLOSURE -15%; OMC/upstream first-order impacts are unchanged. No single company-driver unit sensitivity exceeds 25%/SSU; the >25% cases are event-level and come from chained macro edges (YESBANK -36.7% in EV_HORMUZ_FULL_CLOSURE with order1 = 0 -> -23.5% after these fixes). Note: edge_scale factors multiply any existing edge_overrides factor on the same raw edge.

edge_scale.reason: Double count of RBI intervention. backbone_india models the same mechanism explicitly: F_USDINR -> NEW_FX_RESERVES_IN (-0.9 x US$25bn) -> F_LIQUIDITY_IN (+1.45) = -1.3 lakh cr per +3% INR. The direct edge (-1.0, 'RBI dollar sales drain liquidity') adds a second -1.0, so +3% INR currently drains ~-2.0 lakh cr after damping. It is the 4th-largest driver-edge flow into YESBANK/TATACAP in EV_IRAN_WAR_HORMUZ_OIL (-4.3 of -24.0).

Largest flow-carrying edge in the graph: sum of |path contributions| through it is 1,612, versus 1,093 for the next edge. Central 1.44 SSU = 36bp per +1pp CPI. backbone_india's own evidence (CPI ~2.8% -> 5.5% in 2026 was met by one 25bp hike on 7 Oct) implies ~0.37 SSU/pp realised. Adding the catalogue's priced odds (Dec hike 0.40, Feb hike 0.27) gives ~0.62 SSU/pp expected. RBI looks through supply-led (food, oil) CPI, which is what this graph mostly propagates. Explicit RBI decision events (EV_RBI_DEC26/FEB27/APR27) already carry the policy path, so CPI-shock events double count it. x0.5 gives 0.72 SSU, about 18bp per pp.

Not netted of parallel paths. energy.json 0.5 means +10% Brent -> INR -1.5% on the direct edge alone. backbone_global (0.18) nets out the FPI, CPI and GDP paths and cites an empirical weekly beta of 0.06-0.12. The 2026 episode (Brent +50% y/y, INR +6.5% with record FPI outflow and US tariffs) gives <=0.44 TOTAL. This is the #1 driver edge in the Hormuz events (flow -10.1 into YESBANK, -7.9 into MOTILALOFS). After the fix, the dedup mean is ~0.26.
Same as energy.json: 0.6 central (INR -1.8% per +10% Brent) is a total, not a direct, effect. Brent -> FPI -> INR, Brent -> CPI -> INR and Brent -> GDP paths already exist.

global_macro 0.5 ('INR beta to DXY ~0.5') is a total beta. backbone_global (0.17, high confidence) explicitly nets out the CNY (+0.04) and FPI (+0.05) paths and cites an empirical 3y weekly total of 0.04-0.10. After the fix the dedup mean is ~0.20 (was 0.294).
-0.8 (-US$4bn/qtr per +3% DXY) is twice backbone_global's -0.3. It is also not netted of DXY -> USDINR -> FPI (-0.4) and US_10Y -> DXY co-movement. After the fix the mean is ~-0.35.

Tight feedback pair. F_RISK_SENTIMENT -> F_US_EQUITIES is -0.55 and this reverse edge is -0.6; the loop product is +0.33, the largest 2-cycle in the graph. VIX is the implied vol of the S&P, so the two are one market move, and every upstream shock (US_GDP, FED_FUNDS, US_10Y, AI_CAPEX) reaches companies twice. Example: F_US_GDP -> F_RISK_SENTIMENT (-0.3) direct plus F_US_GDP -> F_US_EQUITIES -> F_RISK_SENTIMENT (-0.54). Flow through this edge is 283. Keep the RISK -> US_EQ direction.

Unit error. +Rs1/l on ~150bn l industry petrol+diesel = Rs15k cr pre-tax. The Government receives ~50% via dividend and tax, ~Rs7.5k cr, which is ~0.7% of central capex (~Rs11-12 lakh cr) -> +0.07 SSU (SSU +10% capex growth), not 0.3. At 0.3, EV_OMC_FUEL_FREEZE_LOSSES (margin -3) cuts government capex growth by 9pp and hits BANKINDIA/SAIL/TMCV/PNB/POWERINDIA by about -3% each. The edge's own text is just 'OMC capex and PSU dividends feed fiscal/capex' (low confidence).

Node conflation. P_WINDFALL_EXPORT_TAX's company edges are fuel/metal windfall taxes (RELIANCE -3.0, HINDZINC -4.0, BPCL -1.5), plus P_WINDFALL -> F_REFINING_MARGIN -0.6. This edge (food export curbs) therefore routes food inflation into a Reliance/Hindustan Zinc tax hit. Food export curbs already have their own node: F_FOOD_INFLATION_IN -> NEW_AGRI_TRADE_CURBS_IN (+0.5, backbone_india).

Companion of the food-curb conflation above. A fuel/metal windfall levy (e.g. EV_EXPORT_LEVY_REVISIONS) does not lower food inflation; NEW_AGRI_TRADE_CURBS_IN -> F_FOOD_INFLATION_IN (-0.2) already carries the food-export-curb effect.

Double count of the fiscal channel. P_FERT_SUBSIDY -> NEW_FISCAL_SLIPPAGE_IN (0.15) -> F_GSEC_10Y_IN (0.5) gives +1.9bp per subsidy step; this direct edge adds +7.5bp, four times the explicit channel. Without the fix, EV_NBS_RABI_HIKE spills -1.1% onto ADANIGREEN and similar rate-sensitive names.

This multiplies the existing x0.1 override (net -0.1). Mortgages are mostly repo-linked (EBLR) and F_REPO_IN -> F_HOUSING_DEMAND (-0.26, 3 sources) already carries them. Repo -> G-sec (0.53) -> housing (-0.3) adds a further 49% through a channel that barely sets home-loan rates. With the fix, +25bp G-sec -> -1% housing sales (HFC/MCLR share).

C_RUSSIA +1 = India's closer trade access/larger discounts. India's purchases do not add or remove barrels from the world market: Russia re-routes at a deeper discount (the mechanism text 'loss of 1.8 mb/d' assumes the barrels vanish). Global sanctions (Oct-2025 Rosneft/Lukoil) moved Brent ~+5%; an India-only shift is a fraction of that. -0.6 -> -0.24 (Brent -2.4% per step). Flow through the edge is 176; it also double-counts OMC discount benefits already on BPCL/IOC/HPCL's own C_RUSSIA edges.

global_macro 0.6 ('China ~50% of steel') is a total effect. backbone_global keeps only the direct 0.15 because the export (CHINA_GDP -> CHINA_STEEL_EXPORTS -> STEEL_GLOBAL, +0.26 after damping), iron-ore (+0.13) and coking-coal (+0.14) paths exist. Result: direct 0.15 after dedup (backbone_global's netted value), total ~0.67 SSU (+6.7% global HRC) per +1pp China GDP.
backbone_global (0.3) explicitly nets the Fed channel (US_GDP -> FED_FUNDS -> US_10Y = 0.36); global_macro 0.8 does not. Result: dedup ~0.31.

0.8 = +12% IEX price per +10% domestic coal cost. backbone_global shows the arithmetic: +10% coal -> +~Rs0.2/kWh variable cost -> IEX +3.75% = 0.25. Spot prices are set by scarcity at the evening peak and imported-coal/gas units, and the convex demand edge (POWER_DEMAND -> POWER_PRICE ~1.07) already carries that. After the fix the mean is ~0.29.

Reverse-causal co-movement ('investor co-movement'). The GOLD -> SILVER edge (1.0, empirical) is the causal direction; this reverse edge makes a +0.25 2-cycle. Silver-only shocks (EV_PRECIOUS_METALS_* shock both nodes anyway) should not move gold financiers or jewellers.

The edge's own text is 'base-metal correlation'. Both metals have their own drivers (F_CHINA_GDP -> ALUMINIUM 0.475, -> COPPER 0.73; DXY; energy transition), so routing copper shocks into HINDALCO/VAML/NATIONALUM counts the common driver twice. Example: EV_CHINA_CEWC_STIMULUS_DEC26 shocks F_CHINA_GDP and F_COPPER together.

Sign error versus the node convention. F_RICE feeds F_FOOD_INFLATION_IN (+0.25) and RADICO/UNITDSPR as a DOMESTIC grain cost. The catalogue's EV_RICE_BROKEN_EXPORT_CURB shocks F_RICE -0.3, so an Indian export curb lowers domestic rice. The +0.4 edge encodes the world-price effect, which makes a food-curb measure RAISE Indian food inflation. Flip and halve: w -0.2, range [-0.75, 0]. If negative factors are not allowed, use factor 0 and add the edge given in findings.

Mechanism text: 'Statistical proxy only ... No direct fundamental link'. Observed gold -1.05 SSU since June books +2.1% 'unpriced' impact for AGEL, and Mideast escalation (via C_MIDEAST -> F_GOLD) books -0.8%/step. Beta and real-yield exposure are carried by F_RISK_SENTIMENT/F_GSEC/F_FPI edges.
Mechanism text says 'likely spurious (period-specific)'. Observed DXY +0.74 SSU books -1.1% for MAXHEALTH with no causal channel.
Mechanism text: 'no direct fundamental channel beyond imported-fuel cost'. The fuel channel belongs to F_USDINR/F_COAL_INTL. Keep -0.5 as a token; observed DXY +0.74 currently books -1.1%.
Mechanism text: 'no fundamental channel for an insurance marketplace'. The observed F_REFINING_MARGIN state is +1.54 (HO=F proxy, see findings), so this edge books +1.2% 'unpriced' upside.
Mechanism text: 'no mechanism; shrunk heavily'. Observed F_STEEL_GLOBAL is +2.06, which books -1.6%.
Mechanism text: 'there is no causal channel ... proxies global-cyclical risk appetite'. Risk appetite is already F_RISK_SENTIMENT/F_US_EQUITIES.
Mechanism text: 'no causal channel; risk-on proxy. Token weight.'
Mechanism text: 'no causal channel (coal is <0.5% of IT costs)'. F_COAL_INTL also receives backbone flows (F_GAS_GLOBAL -> F_COAL_INTL, F_CHINA_GDP -> F_COAL_INTL).
Mechanism text: 'no causal channel; likely data-mined'. Observed sugar +2.78 SSU books +0.8% for OFSS.
Mechanism text: 'no causal channel (cyclical-risk proxy)'. Observed aluminium -1.96 SSU books -0.6%.
Mechanism text: 'no causal channel; included as noise token' (t 1.1, insignificant).

recent_state_overrides.reason: Wrong series and wrong sign. The node is 'Global natural gas / LNG price' and every backbone edge into it is about Asian LNG (Qatar/Hormuz), but the observed state uses NG=F (Henry Hub): -7.0% since 2026-06-01 -> -0.47 SSU. Because observed nodes override event shocks in recent_state(), the catalogue's own EV_LNG_HORMUZ_DISRUPTION (+1.0) is ignored; its what_already_moved text even says NG=F is 'not representative of JKM/TTF'. Asian spot LNG rose from an '11-week high' in June to its highest level since 2022 in mid/late October. Use +1.0 (energy agent's estimate, conservative given the headlines) until a JKM series is wired in. This affects GAIL, ATGL, IOC, HINDPETRO, TATASTEEL, fertiliser and CGD exposure.
recent_state_overrides.evidence: Google News RSS (https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=JKM+LNG+price+Asia+spot+when:30d&hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN:en): 'Asia spot LNG at 11-week high as Middle East tensions and hot weather drive demand' (BOE Report, 2026-06-12); 'Asian spot LNG prices hit highest level in nearly 4 years' (Pipeline and Gas Journal, 2026-10-16); 'Asian LNG Prices Jump to Highest Since 2022 on Tanker Strikes' (Bloomberg, 2026-10-20); 'Asian spot LNG hits highest since 2022 on cold weather, China demand' (Pipeline and Gas Journal, 2026-10-23).

findings.subject: F_CPI_IN -> F_REPO_IN (and banks/NBFCs/realty)
findings.issue: This is the dominant amplifier of the whole graph. F_CPI_IN has order1 |sum| 8.7 but order2 282 and order3 193 across companies. F_FOOD_INFLATION_IN is 94% order 3-4. For every food/CPI event the bank, NBFC and real-estate response runs entirely through CPI -> REPO (36bp/pp) -> {company, G-sec, credit growth, asset quality}. Examples: EV_PULSES_VEG_SPIKE_WINTER -> YESBANK -10.7, BAJFINANCE -9.8, PRESTIGE -8.0; EV_CPI_REACCEL_SEP26 sums to 581 over companies. Forward RBI decisions are already separate exclusive events, so repo moves are counted twice across events. Fix proposed (x0.5). After the full set of fixes, YESBANK goes -10.7 -> -7.1 and EV_CPI_REACCEL_SEP26 581 -> 356.
findings.evidence: results/sensitivity_by_order.csv; backbone_india.json mechanism (2.7pp CPI rise met by one 25bp hike on 2026-10-07); events/dedup.json exclusive_groups for RBI Dec/Feb/Apr.

findings.subject: F_BRENT -> F_USDINR / F_USDINR -> F_LIQUIDITY_IN (Hormuz events)
findings.issue: In EV_IRAN_WAR_HORMUZ_OIL (occurred, |impact| 1,374) and EV_HORMUZ_FULL_CLOSURE, the largest driver-edge flows into the worst-hit financials are, in order: Brent -> USDINR (-10.1 for YESBANK), Brent -> CPI (-7.5), CPI -> REPO (-5.4) and USDINR -> LIQUIDITY (-4.3, plus -2.3 through FX reserves). YESBANK, AUBANK, TATACAP, BAJFINANCE, PRESTIGE and PFC have order1 = 0 yet reach -17% to -37%. Two un-netted Brent -> INR estimates (0.5 and 0.6) and a duplicated intervention-liquidity channel drive this. After the fixes YESBANK goes -36.7 -> -23.5 in Hormuz closure and -24.0 -> -14.7 in the occurred war event.
findings.evidence: Path attribution via mi.graph.Network on catalogue entry shocks (Brent 4.95, Mideast 1.5, Red Sea 1.0, GRM 1.5).

findings.subject: mi/graph.py OVERLAP_DAMP (structural double counting)
findings.issue: OVERLAP_DAMP only fires when the company has a direct edge from the path's START node. Banks and NBFCs carry direct edges to F_REPO_IN, F_GSEC_10Y_IN, F_CREDIT_GROWTH_IN, F_ASSET_QUALITY_IN, F_LIQUIDITY_IN, F_GDP_IN and F_FPI_FLOWS. Paths such as X -> F_GDP_IN -> F_ASSET_QUALITY_IN -> bank or X -> F_REPO_IN -> F_GSEC_10Y_IN -> bank therefore re-count channels the bank's own GDP/REPO edges already embed (profile edges are written as totals). Example: F_RURAL_DEMAND -> INDUSINDBK = +10.1%/SSU with order1 = 0, of which 3.1 is RURAL -> GDP -> ASSET_QUALITY -> bank on top of 2.6 RURAL -> GDP -> bank. Recommend a code change: apply OVERLAP_DAMP once when ANY intermediate node (not only the start) has a direct edge to the terminal company. Measured on top of the edge_scale fixes: EV_CPI_REACCEL_SEP26 356 -> 301 (-15%), EV_IRAN_WAR_HORMUZ_OIL 1153 -> 1061 (-8%), YESBANK CPI-event impact -8.0 -> -6.1. First-order and OMC/upstream impacts are unchanged.

findings.subject: NEW_OMC_MARKETING_MARGIN -> F_GOVT_CAPEX
findings.issue: This is a unit error, about 4-5x too large (see edge_scale). Because the occurred EV_OMC_FUEL_FREEZE_LOSSES shocks margin -3.0, the error books -0.9 SSU of government capex growth: about -3% on PSU banks, SAIL, TMCV and POWERINDIA, and 46% of that event's total |impact| is non-OMC spill-over. In the recent state F_GOVT_CAPEX is clamped, so the damage is in forward events (EV_INDIA_RETAIL_FUEL_HIKE +2.5, EV_LPG_COMPENSATION_CABINET +1.0). For LT, 2.1 of the +1.4% from a retail fuel hike is this edge.

findings.subject: P_WINDFALL_EXPORT_TAX node conflation
findings.issue: One node mixes food export curbs (inbound from F_FOOD_INFLATION_IN) with fuel/metal windfall levies (outbound to RELIANCE -3, HINDZINC -4, BPCL -1.5 and F_REFINING_MARGIN -0.6). Food shocks therefore tax Reliance and Hindustan Zinc. Remove both food edges (edge_scale). The food-curb channel stays on NEW_AGRI_TRADE_CURBS_IN.

findings.subject: F_REFINING_MARGIN observed series (HO=F) and edge_flags.csv
findings.issue: SSU_SCALE converts the NY-Harbor heating-oil futures PRICE (HO=F) at 10% = 1 SSU, but the SSU is '+$2/bbl gross refining margin'. A heating-oil price level co-moves with crude, so (a) the empirical pack sees OMCs fall when 'refining margin' rises. That explains all 3 empirical sign conflicts in edge_flags.csv (BPCL/HINDPETRO/IOC, t -2.8 to -4.1): they are a proxy artefact, so do NOT flip those edges. (b) It produces spurious company edges that agents themselves call non-causal (INFY, HCLTECH, POLICYBZR; zeroed above). (c) The recent state (+1.54 SSU) is not a margin measure: with Brent flat since 1 June the HO - Brent crack moved $57.9 -> $81.4/bbl (+$23.5). Recommend computing the crack in $/bbl (HO x 42 - Brent), mapping it to a complex GRM with ~0.35-0.45 pass-through and dividing by $2. Even the conservative end gives ~+4 SSU (clipped to 3) versus 1.54 today, which would raise RELIANCE/OMC refining contributions; check against Singapore GRM before using it.

findings.subject: Company edges self-described as non-causal (recent-state noise)
findings.issue: At least 30 company edges carry mechanism text saying 'no causal/fundamental channel', 'statistical proxy' or 'spurious'. Most are near zero, but the larger ones turn observed factor moves into 'unpriced impact' for the ranking: F_GOLD -> ADANIGREEN -2.0 (+2.1% from the gold slide), F_DXY -> MAXHEALTH/AMBUJACEM -1.5 (-1.1% each), F_REFINING_MARGIN -> POLICYBZR +0.8 (+1.2%), F_STEEL_GLOBAL -> POLICYBZR -0.8 (-1.6%), F_SUGAR -> OFSS (+0.8%). These are zeroed above. Recommend the assembler drop any company edge whose mechanism declares no causal channel, since the causal graph should not carry empirical-only betas (the beta adjustment already handles market co-movement).
findings.evidence: results/edges_all.csv mechanism column; results/recent_state_vector.csv observed states.

findings.subject: Near-duplicate driver estimates averaged without netting
findings.issue: In several multi-source edges, one file nets out parallel paths and another gives a total beta, and the dedup averages them: Brent -> INR (0.18 vs 0.5/0.6), DXY -> INR (0.17 vs 0.5), DXY -> FPI (-0.3 vs -0.8), China GDP -> global HRC (0.15 vs 0.6), US GDP -> UST10y (0.3 vs 0.8), domestic coal -> IEX (0.25 vs 0.8). All are scaled above. A general fix would be for the assembler to prefer the netted backbone_* estimate when an events/*.json edge for the same pair exceeds it by >2x and has no arithmetic in its mechanism.
findings.evidence: Raw per-origin weights from graph/backbone_*.json and events/*.json.

findings.subject: 2-node cycles
findings.issue: No cycle has |product| >= 1. The largest are RISK <-> US_EQUITIES +0.33 (zeroed), GOLD <-> SILVER +0.25 (zeroed), GDP_IN <-> PRIVATE_CAPEX +0.20, EQUITY_ACTIVITY <-> SEBI_DERIVATIVES -0.23 and CREDIT_GROWTH <-> RBI_PRUDENTIAL -0.17. Simple-path enumeration limits each loop to one traversal, so the remaining loops are acceptable. NEW_FX_RESERVES_IN -> F_USDINR (-0.12) has the confidence-buffer sign, which is opposite to the intervention flow that drives reserves in this graph. It is inert today (no inbound shock except via USDINR, which it cannot loop back to), but should not be used with a reserves-only event.

findings.subject: Near-duplicate company-proposed nodes
findings.issue: These pairs are near-duplicates: NEW_CEMENT_PRICE (+5%, realty cost edges) vs NEW_CEMENT_PRICE_IN (+2.5%, ULTRACEMCO/AMBUJACEM); NEW_WC_COMPETITIVE_INTENSITY (POLYCAB) vs NEW_CABLE_NEW_ENTRANT_PRICING (KEI); NEW_STATE_LIQUOR_POLICY (RADICO) vs NEW_STATE_EXCISE_ALCOHOL (UNITDSPR); NEW_EDIBLE_OIL_IMPORT_DUTY (+5pp, PATANJALI) vs NEW_AGRI_IMPORT_DUTY_IN (+10pp, backbone). None has an inbound edge or event shock today, so there is no double counting yet, but a future event on one will miss its twin. When aliasing, rescale for SSU: NEW_CEMENT_PRICE -> NEW_CEMENT_PRICE_IN needs the realty edges x0.5, and NEW_EDIBLE_OIL_IMPORT_DUTY -> NEW_AGRI_IMPORT_DUTY_IN needs PATANJALI x2.

findings.subject: Macro links checked as present (no ranking-flipping gap found)
findings.issue: These links all exist with sensible signs: Brent -> CPI (0.207, half pass-through because retail prices are frozen) -> repo; USD/INR -> CPI (0.22) -> repo; INR -> every IT exporter (TCS 1.5, INFY 1.5, HCLTECH 1.6, WIPRO 1.8, TECHM 1.8, LTM 2.2, PERSISTENT 2.2, COFORGE/MPHASIS 2.0, OFSS 1.5) and pharma (SUNPHARMA 1.5, DRREDDY 3.2, CIPLA 1.4); China steel exports -> Indian HRC (-0.25 direct, -0.21 via global HRC, +0.1 duty response); repo -> G-sec (0.53); FPI -> INR (-0.23). Sign conventions were verified for F_RISK_SENTIMENT (+ = risk-off; 65 of 69 company edges negative, the positives are BSE/POWERGRID/defensives), F_USDINR (+ = rupee weaker), F_US_GENERIC_PRICING (+ = erosion; all 11 company edges negative) and NEW_SEBI_MF_FEE_REG (+1 = -5bp fee; AMC edges negative). China steel -> India pass-through looks low against 2024 (China exports +23%, Indian HRC ~-14%) but is defensible under the 2025 safeguard duty; it is left unchanged.

findings.subject: Missing link F_DXY -> F_BRENT
findings.issue: DXY feeds gold, copper, aluminium and zinc but not Brent. For forward Fed/UST events (F_DXY not clamped) India loses the partial oil-import offset of a strong dollar. This is a small effect and not ranking-flipping.

proposed_edge.mechanism: Dollar-denominated commodity pricing: +3% DXY -> Brent ~-2.5% (elasticity ~-0.8, unstable since 2020) = -0.25 SSU (SSU +10% Brent). Source: model knowledge.

findings.subject: Corrected edge if negative edge_scale factors are not supported
findings.issue: Replace NEW_AGRI_TRADE_CURBS_IN -> F_RICE (+0.4, backbone_india.json) with the signed domestic-price version below.

proposed_edge.mechanism: An export ban/duty or stock limit on a major grain diverts supply home: domestic rice ~-2% per measure (-0.2 SSU; SSU +10% rice), consistent with EV_RICE_BROKEN_EXPORT_CURB (F_RICE -0.3). The world-price rise is not this node's unit.
